profiling.experiment: 5x4-bitwise, three additional untimed sampling runs; every complete output matched ORT bitwise
profiling.verified_fast_path: Matched QEMU float32_muladd calls fmaf@plt, IFUNC dispatch on this host selects vfmadd213ss. The float32_muladd function also contains IEEE-state checks; its whole-function samples are not pure host FMA cycles.
profiling.vcpu_percent_denominator: All sampled vCPU user-space CPU-clock IPs, across three fresh runs
profiling.host_symbols_source: attribution.json (matched QEMU build ID and libm IFUNC, same raw samples)
notes: Host helper/IP ranges and JIT-site ranges are disjoint for every run/core. Source-line debug entries were zero; instruction boundaries come from perfmap and ELF disassembly.
Perf samples carry IP and thread IDs only. Recycled overlapping JIT host addresses have no recoverable translation order for these samples; 111 retained as ambiguous.

A guest instruction site marks its QEMU-generated host range; the first instruction can include TB entry checks. Out-of-line slow-path code after the final guest instruction range may not appear in the map.
Separate sampling identifies CPU locations; counts are not wall time, cache-miss counts, per-instruction cost, an optimization speedup or a rigorous bound.

native_fma_detail.scope: Address of interrupted host instruction in same-QEMU-process software CPU-clock samples. Categories partition only the preidentified host FMA range. Do not interpret counts as cycles spent executing an instruction or savings obtainable by deleting instructions. Skid and call returns may move IP away from the operation incurring latency.

decision: Keep the previous acceptance candidate and 1.5x threshold. Bitwise FP32 writeback lowered the median from the previous cached 5x4 by 0.48–3.12% in four batches. The best paired-load and bitwise combination did not reproduce its first improvement in the independent fifth batch.
